scope: V4: aortic compliance, arteriolar resistance, LDL origin and plaque sequence

sources.title: Introduction to Lipids and Lipoproteins
sources.author: Kenneth R Feingold
sources.retrieval: Publisher-hosted original PDF successfully read; NCBI HTML returned a browser check and was not counted as read
claims: Liver secretes triglyceride-rich VLDL; lipoprotein lipase removes triglyceride en route to muscle/adipose tissue, forming IDL.
Some IDL is cleared by liver; remaining IDL is further metabolized to LDL.
Plasma LDL depends on production and clearance; hepatic LDL receptors are central to clearance.
LDL particles can bind/trap in the arterial wall; lipid uptake by macrophages supports foam-cell/plaque explanation.

sources.title: Atherosclerosis: Causes and Risk Factors
claims: High blood pressure and unhealthy cholesterol levels are risk factors for atherosclerosis.
Inflammatory cells and cholesterol accumulate; white blood cells consume cholesterol and contribute to plaque.
Plaque disruption can trigger blood clots and impair blood flow.

sources.title: Blood Cholesterol: Causes and Risk Factors
claims: Age, genes, lifestyle, and medical conditions can influence LDL level and hepatic clearance.

sources.title: High Blood Pressure: Causes and Risk Factors
claims: Age, family history, salt sensitivity, kidney disease, sleep and other factors contribute to hypertension risk.

visualConstraints: Aorta compliance animation and arteriolar smooth-muscle resistance animation must use distinct anatomies.
Pressure is force per area at vessel wall; flow occurs under a pressure gradient.
VLDL/IDL/LDL are transport particles, not artery-wall fragments.
IDL-to-LDL is one branch; IDL hepatic uptake is another.
Foam cells and plaque grow within intima; lumen clot follows cap rupture.
Scale-changing micro views must be distinguished from gross anatomical scale.
spokenSimplifications: IDL is referred to as an intermediate stage in narration, but can be labeled IDL on screen.
Lipoprotein-lipase-mediated triglyceride removal is paraphrased as unloading triglycerides.
Foam-cell and fibrous-plaque development are condensed for the five-minute format.
notClaimed: No patient-specific CFD or clinical diagnostic simulation.
No assertion that hypertension generally results from plaque blockage.
